Method of Attack: Allows malicious apps to camouflage as almost any legitimate app by exploiting Android multitasking system weakness (taskAffinity)
Malware can request any permission by disguising as legitimate apps to increase data harvesting
Tricks victims into handing over sensitive information via screen overlays
Can listen to microphone, take photos, read/send SMS, record calls, phish credentials, access private files, location, contacts, and phone logs
Impacted Systems: All versions of Android up to and including Android 10
Attack Vector: Malicious apps exploiting Android multitasking system vulnerability (StrandHogg) without rooting the device
Date of Discovery: StrandHogg vulnerability reported in 2019 (implied by context)
Indicators of Compromise: Malware droppers and downloaders distributed via Google Play Store (removed by Google)
Permission pop-ups without app names, apps asking for unnecessary permissions, UI discrepancies, apps asking to log in again
